The Cotswolds: England at Its Most Refined

The Cotswolds is England's largest Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, stretching across six counties from Chipping Campden in the north to Bath in the south. It's a landscape of rolling wolds, ancient woodland, and honey-coloured stone villages that epitomises the English countryside. For motorcyclists, it offers gentle, flowing roads through some of the country's most photogenic scenery.

The Must-Visit Villages

Castle Combe is regularly voted England's prettiest village — a hidden valley of medieval stone cottages and a 14th-century market cross. Bibury has the famous Arlington Row, a terrace of 14th-century weavers' cottages. Broadway, the Jewel of the Cotswolds, has a wide main street lined with galleries and tearooms.

The Overlooked Gems

  • Snowshill — Tiny hamlet with a National Trust manor house stuffed with eccentric collections
  • Guiting Power — Remote village with excellent pub (the Hollow Bottom) and cricket green
  • Naunton — Hidden in a valley of the River Windrush, barely touristy at all
  • Chedworth — Roman villa in a wooded valley, one of Britain's finest
  • Slad — Laurie Lee's village from Cider with Rosie, with the Woolpack pub

The Best Cotswolds Roads

The B4632 from Broadway to Cheltenham is the escarpment road — sweeping bends with panoramic views east across the Vale of Evesham. The A44 from Moreton-in-Marsh to Chipping Norton flows through classic wold country. For quiet lanes, explore the valleys around the Slaughters and Bourton-on-the-Water where the roads follow the Windrush and Eye rivers.

The Cotswolds is proof that motorcycle touring doesn't need mountain passes or dramatic coastline. Sometimes, a gentle road through a beautiful village is all you need.

Food and Drink

The Cotswolds is a food lover's paradise. Daylesford Farm Shop near Kingham is a temple of organic produce. The pubs serve some of England's best food — try the Wheatsheaf in Northleach, the Five Alls in Filkins, or the Plough Inn at Cold Aston. Local ales from Hook Norton, Donnington, and North Cotswold Brewery are excellent.

Practical Information

The Cotswolds is easily accessible from London (90 minutes), Birmingham (1 hour), and Bristol (45 minutes). Fuel is available in every market town. The area is busiest from June to August, with Bourton-on-the-Water and Broadway experiencing severe congestion on summer weekends. For the best experience, visit in spring (April-May) or autumn (September-October) when the villages are quieter and the light is at its best. faq.q: Which Cotswolds villages should I not miss?
faq.a: Castle Combe is regularly voted England's prettiest village, a hidden valley of medieval stone cottages with a 14th-century market cross. Bibury has the famous Arlington Row, a terrace of 14th-century weavers' cottages, and Broadway, the Jewel of the Cotswolds, has a wide main street lined with galleries and tearooms. For quieter gems, try Snowshill, Naunton and Guiting Power.

faq.q: What are the best roads for motorcycling?
faq.a: The B4632 escarpment road from Broadway to Cheltenham offers sweeping bends with panoramic views east across the Vale of Evesham. The A44 from Moreton-in-Marsh to Chipping Norton flows through classic wold country, and the quiet lanes around the Slaughters and Bourton-on-the-Water follow the Windrush and Eye rivers.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit the Cotswolds?
faq.a: Visit in spring (April-May) or autumn (September-October) when the villages are quieter and the light is at its best. The area is busiest from June to August, with Bourton-on-the-Water and Broadway experiencing severe congestion on summer weekends, which spoils the relaxed riding the Cotswolds are known for.

faq.q: Where should I eat and drink?
faq.a: The Cotswolds is a food lover's paradise. Daylesford Farm Shop near Kingham is a temple of organic produce, and the pubs serve some of England's best food. Try the Wheatsheaf in Northleach, the Five Alls in Filkins or the Plough Inn at Cold Aston, washed down with local ales from Hook Norton or Donnington.

The Cotswolds is easily reached from London in about 90 minutes, Birmingham in an hour and Bristol in 45 minutes, making it ideal for a weekend break. Fuel is available in every market town. The riding is gentle and flowing rather than dramatic, proving that touring does not need mountain passes to be rewarding.
